value.body: Jan Aushadhi Kendras are medicine stores under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) that sell generic medicines supplied by the Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI). Individuals, NGOs, hospitals and others run them, and each must have a pharmacist with a D.Pharm or B.Pharm. For a pharmacist, it is a way to run a store with scheme support, or a job at an existing kendra.

items.label: Pharmacist requirement
items.note: As the applicant or as an employee at the store

items.label: Monthly incentive
items.value: 20% of monthly purchases, up to ₹20,000 a month
items.note: Subject to conditions such as stocking specified medicines

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Apply online on the PMBI portal as an individual pharmacist or entrepreneur, with premises, a retail drug licence (or an application for one) and a D.Pharm or B.Pharm pharmacist. PMBI reviews the application and may inspect the site before onboarding the store. To work at an existing kendra, apply to its owner.

value.title: At a glance
items: This is self-employment under a government scheme, not a government job; income depends on sales.
Generic medicines are priced lower than branded ones, so earnings depend on footfall and steady stock.
A one-time incentive is offered in some regions and to women, ex-servicemen, divyang and SC/ST applicants.
Rules and incentives are revised from time to time; check the current PMBI guidelines.

value.title: Jan Aushadhi Kendras open (cumulative)
value.note: Counts at the end of each financial year (March), except the last, which is as on 30 Nov 2025. Figures are kendras opened, not necessarily all still operating.
value.source: Lok Sabha replies (USQ 1373, Feb 2024; Dec 2025) and PMBJP portal figures as compiled by ORF
